description: Queue base type. A queue is a named dispatch channel; every queue is registered as a GTS well-known instance of this type. The registration carries concurrency limits, a default priority, default timeout values, a default retry policy, optional queue-depth and worker-blacklist settings, optional default progress settings, and an optional dead-letter queue reference. A queue of kind 'dead_letter' is not a dispatch channel: it only holds parked dead_lettered tasks, is never claimable, and declares no dispatch settings. Task domains route by queue; dead-letter queues are not routed, so one dead-letter queue can serve queues in several domains (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-task-domains). Values declared here are defaults that operators MAY override in the Task Engine config file by GTS queue pattern (most specific pattern wins). Trait/field keys use snake_case per platform GTS convention.

id.description: Full GTS queue identifier (e.g. gts.cf.core.tasks.queue.v1~cf.core.tasks.default.v1). An instance, so it never ends in '~'.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the queue carries. ASCII only.

kind.description: 'dispatch' (default): a normal queue that workers claim from. 'dead_letter': holds parked dead_lettered tasks only (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-dead-letter); it is never dispatched, a claim naming it is rejected 400 invalid_argument, and it MUST NOT declare any dispatch setting (concurrency, priority, timeouts, retry, depth, blacklist, progress, fairness, dead_letter_queue, operated_by, accepted_types).

global_concurrency_limit.description: Maximum number of simultaneously executing (claimed + running) tasks from this queue across all tenants. 0 means unlimited (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-queue-concurrency).

per_tenant_concurrency_limit.description: Maximum number of simultaneously executing (claimed + running) tasks from this queue per tenant. 0 means unlimited.

default_priority.description: Default task priority for tasks enqueued to this queue when the creator supplies none. Range 0 (highest) to 1000 (lowest), the same range as task priority (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-priority-dispatch). Priority orders one tenant's own tasks only; it never ranks one tenant above another.

timeouts.description: Default timeout values applied to tasks on this queue when the task itself declares none. All values are in seconds. null/absent means 'no timeout of that kind' for every field except heartbeat_timeout_secs and execution_timeout_secs: a claimed task always has a lease, so null there means 'use the engine default lease' (default_lease_duration_secs); and every task has an execution timeout, so null there means 'use the engine default' (default_execution_timeout_secs).

queue_timeout_secs.description: Maximum time a task may wait in 'queued' before it is force-completed as timed out (terminal).

assignment_timeout_secs.description: Maximum time a claimed task may remain 'claimed' before it starts (assignment_deadline); on expiry it is a liveness failure and the task is requeued with backoff against max_liveness_requeues (not max_retries).

execution_timeout_secs.description: Maximum running time per attempt (execution_deadline, re-armed on each start so time spent waiting is never counted). Terminal, task-attributed, never retried. Every task has an execution timeout: null/absent here falls through to the next level (task request, then type trait, then queue) and finally to the engine default default_execution_timeout_secs; it never means 'no limit'. Values above the engine trust limit (trust_limits max_execution_timeout_secs, tighter for tenant-owned types) make the type non-creatable or the queue refuse new tasks (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-timeouts, cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-type-trust).

heartbeat_timeout_secs.description: Lease duration: the maximum interval between worker heartbeats before the lease expires; falls back to default_lease_duration_secs when null. Workers MUST heartbeat at the heartbeat_interval_secs returned on claim (one third of this value, rounded down, minimum 1) so a single delayed heartbeat does not expire the lease. A lease below the engine minimum (config trust_limits.min_lease_secs, default 10) makes the queue refuse new tasks (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-type-trust). An expired lease is a liveness failure: the task is requeued with backoff against max_liveness_requeues (not max_retries).

lifetime_timeout_secs.description: Absolute wall-clock budget from creation to terminal state, surviving requeues. On expiry the task is force-completed as timed out (overrides retry/lease handling).

retry_policy.description: Default retry policy for tasks on this queue when the task declares none.

max_retries.description: Maximum number of retries after explicit retryable failures reported by a worker. Liveness requeues (lease expiry, assignment timeout) do not consume this budget; see max_liveness_requeues.

max_liveness_requeues.description: Maximum number of liveness requeues (lease expiry or assignment timeout) before the task is routed terminally with a timed_out result. Counted separately from max_retries so losing the worker never burns the failure-retry budget. Backoff uses this policy's strategy and intervals, applied to the liveness-requeue count. 0 means unlimited (bounded only by the lifetime timeout, if any).

strategy.description: Backoff strategy used to compute run_after for a retry.

max_interval_secs.description: Maximum backoff interval in seconds (caps exponential/linear growth). MUST be greater than or equal to base_interval_secs; the engine rejects a queue whose policy breaks this rule when it resolves the queue (JSON Schema cannot compare two fields).

jitter_factor.description: Fractional jitter (0.0-1.0) to de-synchronize retries. Jitter only shortens a wait: each wait is drawn from [d * (1 - jitter_factor), d], where d is the capped backoff, so it never exceeds max_interval_secs. 1.0 gives full jitter (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-retry, Backoff).

non_retryable_codes.description: Error codes that are always terminal regardless of the worker's retryable flag.

queue_max_queue_depth.description: Maximum 'queued' tasks in this queue across all tenants. 0 means unlimited. When omitted, the config default queue_depth.queue_max_queue_depth applies (shipped value 1,000,000); overridable in config. The name matches that config key and its siblings tenant_max_queue_depth and global_max_queue_depth.

blacklist_failure_threshold.description: Consecutive worker failures on this queue that trigger a worker blacklisting (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-worker-blacklist). When omitted, the config default blacklist_failure_threshold applies; the schema default shows the shipped value.

blacklist_duration_minutes.description: How long a blacklisted worker is excluded from claiming on this queue. When omitted, the config default blacklist_duration_minutes applies; the schema default shows the shipped value.

progress_events.description: Default progress event mode for tasks on this queue (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-progress-events): 'none', 'milestones', or 'all'. Lower precedence than task-type traits and config overrides. When omitted, the global default applies ('none').

progress_flush_interval_secs.description: Default progress flush interval (seconds) for tasks on this queue. Effective value is clamped to progress_min_flush_interval_secs. When omitted, the config default progress_flush_interval_secs applies; the schema default shows the shipped value.

tenant_fairness.description: How tasks of different tenants are ordered within one urgency class (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-tenant-fairness, cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-priority-dispatch). 'round_robin' (default): tenants take turns; each turn takes that tenant's best task (highest priority, then oldest), so priority only reorders a tenant's own tasks. 'fifo': all tenants' tasks ordered together by priority, then age; because priority then ranks tenants against each other, use it only for single-tenant or trusted queues. Urgency 'critical' always comes first. Overridable in config by queue pattern.

dead_letter_queue.description: Optional GTS identifier of the queue that tasks are dead-lettered into when they exhaust retries or exceed their lifetime. MUST reference a queue of kind 'dead_letter' (checked by the engine when it resolves the queue). It may be shared by queues in different task domains: a dead-lettered task stays in its source queue's database. Absent means failing tasks transition to 'failed' instead of being dead-lettered.

operated_by.description: Who runs this queue's workers (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-worker-principals). 'tenant' (default): tenant workers; claims respect tenant barriers. 'platform': platform workers; a claim may cross tenant barriers if the PDP allows it, and tenant-owned task types cannot be placed here (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-type-trust).

accepted_types.description: Optional task types this queue accepts. Each entry is a GTS task type identifier and also covers the types derived from it (GTS §10). Create, bulk move, and re-enqueue of another type are rejected 400 invalid_argument (PRD cpt-cf-task-engine-fr-type-trust).

then.$comment: Dead-letter queues carry no dispatch settings.
